newsitem.title: USA: Conoco, Maraven close $1.45bn Petrozuata financing.
newsitem.headline: Conoco, Maraven close $1.45bn Petrozuata financing.

text.p: E.I. Dupont de Nemours & Co energy unit Conoco and Petroleos de Venezuela subsidiary Maraven closed $1.45 billion in financing for their closely watched $2.2 billion Petrozuata oil project, a Conoco official said on Monday.

"After much planning and hard work, we closed on Friday June 27 the largest Latin American project financing that's been done to date," Michael Espinosa, assistant treasurer at Conoco, said in a conference call with reporters.
The financing includes a $1 billion bond issue and $450 million in commercial bank financing.
The bond offering, originally pegged at $650 million, was increased to $1 billion in response to strong investor demand, Espinosa said.
The bonds were oversubscribed by a ratio of nine to one, he said.

The first tranche of bonds due April 1, 2009 totaled $300 million and were priced at 120 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. The second tranche due 2017 came to $625 million and was priced 145 basis points over, while the third tranche due 2022 totaling $75 million was priced 160 basis points over.
The bonds were rated Baa1 by Moody's Investors Service, triple-B minus by Standard & Poors and triple-B plus by Duff & Phelps.

Petrozuata, a 50-50 joint venture, is the most advanced of six similar projects worth an estimated $15 billion to upgrade Venezuelan extra heavy crude oil into more marketable "synthetic" crude for export.
Conoco and Maraven earlier this year named CS First Boston and Citibank as lead and co-lead, respectively, of the bond offering.

"This has redefined the way people are going to look at financing projects in emerging markets," said Bayo Ogunlesi, managing director and head of global project financing at CS First Boston. "The project sets and excellent benchmark for the other projects."

Credit Suisse, ING Barings, Nationsbank, Union Bank of Switzerland and the Export Development Corp of Canada are the arrangers for the commercial bank loan. The Petrozuata project will upgrade 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) of the extra heavy crude from the country's vast Orinoco Oil Belt into 102,000 bpd of 20 API gravity synthetic crude for export to the U.S.
Conoco's Lake Charles, Louisiana refinery will take 63,000 bpd of the syncrude. Conoco will sell the balance to Maraven for its Cardon refinery in Venezuela.
The Tar Belt, known in Spanish as the Faja, contains an estimated 270 bilion barrels of recoverable reserves.
